title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Scheduling, Profiling & Runbooks
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical team wiki for Redwood's serving runtime. It consolidates the runtime architecture overview, kernel scheduling design, profiling & benchmarking playbooks, release notes, known issues, operational runbooks, and links to deeper design docs. It is intended for engineers and SREs working on model serving, scheduling, and performance optimization.

Key services and binaries
- redwood-serving: main inference process (C++/CUDA).
- inference-router: request router & policy engine (Go).
- kv-cache: prefix/KV cache service for hot-token reuse (Rust).
- batch-worker: batching coalescer & dispatcher (Python + C++ bindings).
- perf-collector: tracing/metrics agent (internal agent exporting to PerfDB)

Runtime architecture (high level)
- Input flow: request -> inference-router -> candidate model selection -> batch-worker -> redwood-serving instance(s) -> kv-cache checks -> device kernel execution -> response streaming.
- Process model: each GPU hosts one redwood-serving process with worker threads: io-thread, scheduler-thread, execution-thread-pool, cache-fetch threads.
- Sidecars & agents: perf-collector and health-probe run as sidecars for metrics and liveness checks.

Design goals and SLOs
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for seq_len<=512 on production 8xA100 dedicated pools.
- Throughput target: 1200 tokens/sec per A100-40GB GPU for baseline quantized models (varies by model family).
- Error budget & availability: 99.95% uptime for Dedicated pools; 99.9% for Hosted API.

Kernel scheduling and execution model
- Scheduling tiers: realtime (latency-sensitive, small-batch), throughput (large-batch), background (quantization tasks, compactions).
- Scheduling policy: weighted fair queueing with latency-priority preemption. Each request is scored by policy engine (latency_target, cost_budget, customer_tier) and mapped to a scheduling queue.
- Kernel selection: runtime chooses kernels (fused attention, flash attention variants) at runtime using model profile + heuristic table. Kernel selection table is versioned and lives in /etc/redwood/kernel-profiles.json.
- Preemption & eviction: long-running throughput batches can be preempted when realtime queue backlog exceeds threshold (default: 75 pending realtime requests).
- GPU resource isolation: CUDA streams + per-stream mempools to reduce cross-request interference. We pin critical threads to dedicated cores to avoid host-side jitter.

Profiling playbook (when a performance regression is suspected)
1) Reproduce: run the same model, sequence length, and batch size on a staging cluster using perfbench harness. Command: `./perfbench --model /models/ggml-rlhf-q8 --seq 512 --batch 8 --duration 300`
2) Collect traces: enable perf-collector tracing for a 60s window. `kubectl exec -n serving perf-collector -- collect --trace 60s --out /tmp/trace.zip`
3) Capture GPU metrics: nvprof/nsys or nvidia-smi dmon. Example: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run --trace=cuda --duration 60s ./run-sample`
4) Flamegraphs & timeline: upload trace.zip to internal PerfDB and generate flamegraphs. Inspect time spent in: kernel launches, memcpy (H2D/D2H), attention kernels, decoder-step host-side processing.
5) Kernel mismatch checks: compare used kernel ids against kernel-profiles.json for given model and sequence length.
6) Mitigation steps (ordered):
  a) Check batching configuration (max_batch_size, batch_timeout_ms) in route config.
  b) Verify KV cache hits (cache-hit-rate < 70% triggers investigation).
  c) Force alternative kernel via runtime toggle: `redwood-serving --kernel-override attention:flash_v2` and re-run perfbench.
  d) If host CPU is saturated, increase CPU pinning or move perf-collector to a different coreset.

Benchmarking suite (perfbench)
- Purpose: deterministic microbenchmarks and workload-simulating macros to measure token/sec, latency distributions, and throughput across model variants and quantization profiles.
- Test categories:
  - Micro: single-token decode latency, KV-cache lookup latency, attention-kernel latency.
  - Macro: 1k concurrent users simulation, sustained 30m run.
  - Regression: run curated eval prompt set to validate output correctness under quantization.
- CI integration: perfbench runs on nightly smoke cluster with results stored in PerfDB. Alerts fire when p95 changes by >10% relative to baseline.

Release notes (high level)
- v2026.02.18 (canary -> prod):
  - Kernel profile v3.1: added fused flash_v2 kernels for LLaMA-like models; avg p95 reduced 12% on seq<=512.
  - Improved scheduling policy: latency-priority preemption added to reduce tail latencies under bursty traffic.
  - Bugfix: mempool leak during long-running throughput batches resolved.
- Rollout plan: canary (5% clusters) -> staged 25% -> 50% -> full. Auto-rollback on error rate spike >2x baseline or latency p95 regression >15%.

Known issues (tracked)
- Issue #4532: intermittent p99 spikes when kv-cache hit-rate falls below 30% due to cache sharding imbalance. Workaround: increase cache-shard-count to 16 for affected pools.
- Issue #4670: rare OOM on mixed-precision kernels with combined sequence length >2048; mitigation: cap dynamic_seq_limit to 2048 in route config.
- Issue #4721: perf-collector occasionally delays health pings under CPU pressure; recommended to move perf-collector to dedicated cpuset.

Operational runbooks (quick links)
- High latency incident (p95 > 200ms):
  1) Run `perfbench` against canary pool to confirm regression.
  2) Check scheduler queue depths: `kubectl exec -n serving inference-router -- curl localhost:9000/queues` and inspect realtime backlog.
  3) If realtime backlog > 75, scale up realtime pool (manual): `terraform apply -var 'realtime_capacity=10'` or trigger autoscale policy for Dedicated.
  4) If rollout just completed, rollback to previous kernel-profile in /etc/redwood/kernel-profiles.json and restart redwood-serving on canary nodes.
- OOM during decode: evict largest batch, reduce max_batch_size to safe value, and restart workloads on affected pods with `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/redwood-serving`.

Team wiki & ownership
- Primary owners: Runtime team (runtime@redwood.com), oncall rotation: runtime-sre.
- Oncall playbook link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Docs to read first: runtime-architecture-and-profiling-playbook-2026.json, serving-runtime-kernel-scheduling-profiling-and-benchmarking-playbook-2026.json

Operational knobs (config table)
- max_batch_size: default 16; range [1,256]; effect: throughput vs latency trade-off.
- batch_timeout_ms: default 12ms; range [1,200]; effect: waiting time to form batch.
- dynamic_seq_limit: default 2048; cap for dynamic kernel selection.
- cache_shard_count: default 8; recommended 16 for large pools.
- kernel_profile_version: default v3.1; update via canary rollout.

Appendix: Troubleshooting checklist (short)
- If latency regression: verify kernel profile, batching config, kv-cache hit rate, CPU saturation, and recent rollouts.
- If throughput drop: validate GPU utilization (nvidia-smi), check for memcpy hotspots in traces, and ensure batch coalescer is healthy.
- If correctness regression after quantization: run regression triage harness and revert quantization profile.

Contact and escalation
- Runtime owners: runtime@redwood.com (primary), runtime-oncall Slack channel (#runtime-oncall).
- For security/confidential incidents escalate to Security: security@redwood.com.
